title: Possible {name} in source
description: The file contains {name}. A committed token grants its scopes to anyone who can read the repository or artifact until it is revoked. Shape-only: the match does not prove the token is live.
remediation: Revoke the token in the provider console, audit the actions it performed, and issue a minimally scoped replacement that is injected at run time.
limitation: Shape-only: a 20+ character token-shaped literal assigned to a token-named key. It cannot prove the token is valid or unrevoked.
fp: Documentation snippets and example configurations that use the same variable name with placeholder bodies are the common false positives; the rule vetoes EXAMPLE text and requires 20+ characters with a digit.
recordDesc: {name} committed in source is a bearer credential: every reader can call the provider with the token's scopes until it is revoked. Revocation, not deletion of the file, is what ends the exposure.
applicability: Source, CI configuration, deployment manifests and notebooks that may embed {name}.
risk: API access with the token's scopes, including data read/write or infrastructure changes; HIGH severity.
why: {name} stored in the tree works for anyone holding it until the provider revokes it.
fix: Revoke the token at the provider.
Audit the API calls it made and remediate anything unexpected.
Issue a minimal-scope replacement held in a secret manager.
verifyT: The revoked token returns an authentication error and no token-shaped literal remains at this name.
